reader.requirement: When an I-O condition qualifies for a USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION/ERROR declarative in a nest of contained programs, exactly one declarative runs: the one in the program containing the statement (file-name or open-mode form) if it qualifies, otherwise the first GLOBAL declarative found walking outward one directly containing program at a time to the outermost, which must itself satisfy its own execution rules (the same file connector, or the open mode INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND); a non-GLOBAL declarative of a containing program is never selected and, with none found, none runs; a separately compiled program is never reached.

The only switch nearby is EcState.Active (whether any exception-condition feature is in use, not the edition), which picks the int or bool form of the same tiers and the same outward walk

reader.notes: Each program's __IoCheck runs its own file-name tier then open-mode tier (UseTierEmitter), then, when a container in the chain has a GLOBAL declarative, calls __outer.__RunGlobalUse, which runs the same tiers over GLOBAL declaratives only and continues outward. The file key is the connector's own key, so a shadowing local file does not match the outer GLOBAL file's declarative. USE BEFORE REPORTING precedence (X.5.6.4) is a separate rule on ReportWriterEmitter and was not judged here.

refuter.evidence: r4a.cob at --std 85 has a GLOBAL file and a GLOBAL FILE STATUS. N1 (no declaratives) fails OPEN INPUT and only the outer non-GLOBAL USE ON GF exists: none runs (N1 35). N2's own non-GLOBAL open-mode INPUT declarative wins by rule a (N2-INPUT 35). N4's failure skips N3's GLOBAL OUTPUT declarative, which does not satisfy its own execution rules, and selects N3's GLOBAL INPUT one (N3-G-INPUT 35). The outer's own OPEN runs its non-GLOBAL USE ON GF (OUTER-L 35). r4c.cob covers RELATIVE random and INDEXED dynamic files, with INVALID KEY conditions (23, 22) in an inner program: the middle program's GLOBAL I-O declarative is selected first and the outer GLOBAL file-name declarative on the same file is never reached. A READ with an INVALID KEY phrase runs no declarative. Only the first qualifying declarative runs.
